question: Refer to the exhibit. A network engineer must improve the convergence time during vPC primary peer device failure and recovery. Which set of actions is required on both vPC switches to accomplish this task?
context: Topology: two spine switches connect to a vPC Domain (two switches, L3/L2 boundary), which connects to two downstream access switches via vPC 10 and vPC 20.
imageNote: Diagram: two spine switches connect to a vPC Domain (two switches at the L3/L2 boundary), which connects down to two downstream access switches via vPC 10 and vPC 20.
options: Configure the same system priority. Enable LACP toward the access switches.
Configure the same STP priority. Enable the peer-switch feature.
Configure vPC role priority. Enable the peer-gateway feature.
Configure port channels with BPDU guard. Globally enable the loop guard feature.
theory: The vPC peer-switch feature lets both vPC peer devices present the same Spanning Tree bridge ID to downstream switches, so during a primary-peer failure or its later recovery, the secondary doesn't need to renegotiate a new STP root or topology, since both switches were already advertising a shared identity — dramatically reducing the convergence time that would otherwise occur. Configuring identical STP priority on both switches is a prerequisite for enabling peer-switch, since spanning tree needs one consistent root bridge ID between what appear to be two physical switches acting as one logical bridge, whereas BPDU/loop guard and role priority/peer-gateway address different, unrelated failure scenarios. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Peer-Switch and STP Convergence)
